_comment: 305-sta GPS deg-15 probe: KEEP the lane carry, make it fast (LF-1 knobs).
The companion arm (_agu305_gps_d15_nolane_smoke) asks 'what if we drop the lane
carry entirely'.  This one asks 'what does it cost if we keep it', by arming the
two LF-1 optimizations that already exist and ship OFF:
network.lane_carry.parallel_components — fans the per-epoch lane folds across
cores, one component per thread.  Documented BYTE-IDENTICAL to serial (the
only lane knob that is).  Ceiling here is low: the K_c histogram shows ~3
components per epoch (1 tiny + 2 in the 256+ bucket), so expect ~2x at best.
network.lane_carry.fold_blocked — hoists the per-row re-symmetrize to ONE pass
per block per epoch.  That symmetrize is `blk.Pz = (0.5*(Pz + Pz^T)).eval()`
on a 2K x 2K = 7732^2 (478 MB) block, i.e. ~1.4 GB of memory traffic PER ROW
on top of the ~1 GB the rank-1 downdate itself moves -- so it is roughly half
the per-row cost.  NOT bit-identical: it changes operation order and lands in
the parallel_carry equivalence class (<=1e-12 vs sequential, per the card).
GRADE: wall per settled epoch (read from epoch 4 on), and — because fold_blocked
is not bit-identical — the products/solve must be compared, not assumed equal.
NOTE the deeper fix this arm does NOT make: the downdate is written as a full
dense `blk.Pz -= (Ph * Ph.transpose()) / S`.  As a triangular BLAS-2
`Pz.selfadjointView<Lower>().rankUpdate(Ph, -1/S)` it would move half the memory
AND stay exactly symmetric, making the re-symmetrize unnecessary rather than
merely hoisted.  That is a code card with its own LF-1 gates, not a config arm.
